lesson.title: Blending a Whole Set of New Words
lesson.subject: ela

contentBlocks.text: You know seven letters now: S, M, A, T, P, I, N. Today, use all of them together to blend a whole set of brand-new words!

Blend each of these words, sound by sound, then faster until they click into place: man (m-a-n), tan (t-a-n), tap (t-a-p), tip (t-i-p), sap (s-a-p). Notice how many different real words you can make from just seven letters, by changing which letters you use and in what order.
You just blended five brand-new words using only letters you already know! Tomorrow we'll review everything and read real sentences together.

objectives: Blend five new CVC words (man, tan, tap, tip, sap) using this week's and last week's letters
Recognize that a small set of letters can form many different real words
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review all seven letters learned so far (S, M, A, T, P, I, N).
2. Blend each of the five new words together, slowly then faster.
3. Move to the worksheet: trace and blend each word.
4. Discuss how many words came from just seven letters.
5. Close by having the child pick their favorite new word from today and use it in a spoken sentence.
differentiationTips: Struggling: blend just 2-3 of the five words today, saving the rest for extra practice on review day
Ready for more: ask the child to think of one more real word using only letters from this set (S, M, A, T, P, I, N)
This lesson's real payoff is the volume — explicitly point out how many words came from so few letters
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is a tracing and blending activity — check that the child can successfully blend all five words: man, tan, tap, tip, sap.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses the synthetic-phonics goal of this two-week sequence: demonstrating that a small, deliberately chosen letter set unlocks many real, readable words.

worksheet.title: Blending a Whole Set of New Words

generationData.instructions: Trace each word, blend it out loud, then write it once more on your own.
